B1 is remediated in this governance block by authorizing TEST-F04-AC-006 BASELINE_FIXTURE_REBIND from BS-P1-004 to BS-P1-006. B2-B4 remain contract-affecting and block Product implementation: action arg source_kinds are not fixed; input.select options cannot be represented exactly by the frozen F02 TypeDescriptor/TargetMatcher contract; input.select/input.text node-derived event payloads do not have a frozen generated-machine representation.
evidence: B1 — BS-P1-006 F04 §9 requires validator-registry.ts top-level canonical keys registry_version / registry_digest with sha256: digest, while CLOSED T001 TEST-F04-AC-006 still asserts registryVersion / registryDigest. validate-test-integrity permits later-task maintenance only through an explicit BASELINE_FIXTURE_REBIND authorization. This governance block adds that authorization for T002; no test code is changed here.

B2 — F04 FieldContract requires explicit source_kinds in generated machine truth, but logic.random sample_number/choose_item and logic.score increment/set action args omit source_kinds; the only documented shorthand default applies to props. Choosing LITERAL-only versus broader source kinds changes admission behavior.

B3 — input.select.options is specified as LIST<RECORD{label: STRING(120), value: ONE_OF<NUMBER,STRING,BOOLEAN>}>(500), but F02 TypeDescriptor has no ONE_OF variant and F04 TargetMatcher lacks a per-record-field matcher. Because the field is LITERAL-only and composite LITERAL requires a unique concrete expected TypeDescriptor, implementation cannot select a representation without changing admission semantics.

B4 — F04 §9 requires event payload to be a resolved F02 TypeDescriptor, yet input.select.change payload derives from SELECT_ENUM_DOMAIN at node validation time and input.text.change derives from bound state + prop.max_length. The generated artifact representation for these node-derived descriptors is not frozen.
